newsitem.title: CHINA: China optimistic Airbus to join project.
newsitem.headline: China optimistic Airbus to join project.

text.p: China is optimistic that European aviation consortium Airbus Industrie will join a China-led venture to build a 100-seat regional pasenger jet, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

Zhu Yuli, president of China's state-run Aviation Industries of China (AVIC), was optimistic Airbus would join the AE100 project, to be developed by AVIC, Aero International Asia and Singapore Technologies Aerospace.
"Sources with both the Aviation Industries of China (AVIC) and Airbus Industrie have confirmed that talks are underway for the latter's participation in the AE100 programme," Xinhua said.
An official of France's Societe Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, which is a senior partner in Airbus, said on Tuesday that a final agreement had yet to be signed.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, is the other senior partner in Airbus.
China has been courting Airbus to join in the venture, which has been valued at $2.0 billion, since a South Korean firm pulled out of the project last June.

"Airbus' advanced manufacturing technologies and mature marketing system will help enhance the competitiveness of the new plane," Xinhua quoted director of AVIC's international cooperation and trade department Tang Xiaoping as saying.
Zhu said Airbus's participation would not change the share pattern in the project, but gave no details.
China has said it will hold a 46 percent stake in the project while Aero Internationale Asia (AIA) would have 39 percent and Singapore Technologies 15 percent.
AIA is made up of Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Italy's Alenia, a unit of Finmeccanica SpA.
